evidence_quotes.quid_pro_quo: MISSING — Calvin jumps directly to 'What was the preferred move date?' with no time-boxed framing or promise confirmation.
evidence_quotes.their_agenda: MISSING — Never asked 'What are your biggest concerns about this move?' Instead probing starts immediately.
evidence_quotes.two_layers_deep: N/A — No concerns were raised by customer; when damage coverage question emerged, Calvin answered thoroughly without needing to probe deeper.
evidence_quotes.active_listening_reflection: N/A — No concerns summary needed; customer's damage question was answered directly.
evidence_quotes.logistics_details_gathered: Property type (two 4-bedroom houses), floors (2-story both), rooms (4 bedrooms + game room), walking distance ('short walks'), special items (arcade machine, freezer, TVs), additional stops (implicit in two addresses). All substantially covered.
evidence_quotes.estimate_anchor: Yes, rate ($460/hr), trip fee ($115 per truck), estimated time (6.75 hours = $3,335), 15-min increments, and personalization to arcade machine and house size: 'especially with the arcade machine and some larger items and the size of the house and number of bedrooms. Probably best bet is a four man crew.'
evidence_quotes.pricing_framing: Both present — Trip fee disclosed upfront ('$115 each truck to get back'), 15-minute increment billing disclosed ('we bill in fifteen minute increment you only pay for time used'), no deposit/cancellation fee mentioned, and tax/credit card fee note: 'no taxes and no credit card fees.'
evidence_quotes.feels_fair_then_silence: NOT ASKED — After giving the estimate, Calvin moves directly to arrival time and next steps without asking 'Does that feel fair?' or pausing for reaction.
evidence_quotes.on_time_guarantee_delivered: NONE — Never mentioned. Calvin discusses damage coverage but no on-time discount or lateness guarantee.
evidence_quotes.damage_coverage_delivered: FULL — 'no worries, damage coverage. Which is included in the hourly rate. It allocates up to $2,000 per move' + 'no worries damage coverage is no extra cost to, to you' + emphasis on replacement/reimbursement over dollar settlements. All key terms covered.
evidence_quotes.closes_the_loop: FALSE — After damage coverage explanation, customer immediately raises time-estimate concern ('your time estimate seems high'), and Calvin addresses that. No explicit close like 'Does that put those to rest?' and no attempt to avoid repeating already-covered material.
evidence_quotes.final_concerns_check: FULL — 'while we're on the phone any other questions or concerns?' Genuine phrasing, not a throwaway 'any questions.'
evidence_quotes.followup_on_remaining_concern: FULL — Customer raises damage question and Calvin goes in-depth (background checks, W-2 employees, $60/lb standard, $2K no-deductible coverage, replacement reimbursement). Then customer raises time-estimate concern and Calvin follows up: 'if you did have, like I said, the inventory or some pictures, I can re address it and see if you know, one truck and if two guys would be able to do it.'
evidence_quotes.catch_all_asked: FALSE — Never asked 'Anything coming with you we haven't talked about?'
evidence_quotes.explicit_ask: FULL — 'So as it stands now I'm on the schedule' — customer confirms; Calvin never softens with 'or I can email this over' or similar out.
evidence_quotes.rate_lock_mentioned: FALSE — No mention of rate-lock, price-hold, or commitment terms.
evidence_quotes.booking_confirmed: FULL — Date (October 24th), phone number (confirmed earlier), arrival window (8:30–9:00 AM), crew size (two trucks, 4-man crew), both addresses (11000 Roderick Lasson Lane to 16323 [second address]), and notes about insurance/damage coverage and arcade machine sent in confirmation email. All key booking details confirmed.

top_strength: Calvin gathered comprehensive logistics details (4-bedroom homes, arcade machine, freezer, 2-story structure, short walks) and delivered thorough, confident damage coverage explanation that directly answered the customer's most pressing concern about liability.
coaching_note: Critical gap: never frame the call with the quid pro quo ('10–15 minutes, you'll walk away with a quote you can depend on, does that sound good?') and never ask their agenda upfront before diving into probing—these omissions cost discovery quality and rapport-building that should anchor a standard sales call.
